program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 1500

source_provenance: collision screening against merged history, pending Waves 501-1000, and active Waves 1001-1400

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 1500

waves.focus: Randomized double-blind trial in nasopharyngeal-cancer chemoradiotherapy found intravenous vitamin C did not reduce gastrointestinal treatment toxicities, although platelet-count decline was attenuated; supportive hematologic signal without broad toxicity reduction.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of contemporary scurvy in high-income countries found cases clustered in vulnerable people with restrictive diets, neurodevelopmental disorders, medical complexity and psychosocial risk; useful deficiency-risk context rather than supplementation efficacy.

Twelve-month randomized trial in high-cardiovascular-risk adults found an Ayurvedic herbal formulation improved endothelium-independent dilation versus placebo, while vitamin C/E did not clearly outperform placebo on the main vascular endpoints; multi-arm comparison does not support a C/E vascular benefit.

Multicenter phase-3 VICTORY trial in severe burns was stopped early for futility/harm: high-dose intravenous vitamin C did not improve discharge or organ outcomes and the primary mortality/persistent-organ-dysfunction composite numerically favored placebo.

Multicenter randomized VITaCCA trial found intravenous vitamin C did not improve post-cardiac-arrest organ dysfunction; the 10-g dose produced worse R-SOFA change, renal function, troponin release and neurological outcomes than placebo.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of 15 interventions found ascorbate-rich fruits consumed with meals improved ferritin, hemoglobin and transferrin-receptor measures, while direct fractional iron-absorption evidence was not clearly significant; food-matrix evidence should not be reduced to isolated vitamin C dosing.

Small double-blind crossover T2D trial found four months of vitamin C altered multiple plasma proteins and pathways related to innate immunity and metabolism; proteomic changes were mechanistic and do not by themselves establish clinical benefit.

Umbrella review of 31 sepsis/septic-shock reviews found vitamin-C combination regimens did not reduce mortality and hemodynamic improvements were modest; monotherapy mortality signals were low-to-moderate certainty and highly context-dependent.

Large randomized trial in 710 CKD patients undergoing kidney biopsy found perioperative intravenous vitamin C did not reduce perirenal hematoma size, pain or bleeding complications, arguing against routine prophylactic use in this setting.

Meta-analysis of eight randomized COVID-19 trials involving 2,104 patients found no significant mortality reduction with high-dose vitamin C overall; study-level heterogeneity prevents a definitive benefit claim.

Small open-label randomized trial in older adults found a commercial fruit/vegetable/berry powder was metabolically tolerated and improved selected oxidative and blood-pressure markers, but several effects attenuated after covariate adjustment and the formulation is proprietary.

Updated meta-analysis of 14 sepsis/septic-shock RCTs found a mortality signal for intravenous vitamin C, but evidence quality was low and the apparent benefit was driven by single-center rather than multicenter trials; larger low-bias trials remain inconclusive.

Phase-2 placebo-controlled EVITA trial found oral vitamin C did not change the primary clonal-growth endpoint in CCUS/lower-risk myeloid disease; exploratory cytokine, serious-adverse-event and survival signals require phase-3 confirmation.

Meta-analysis of five RCTs found tocotrienol-rich vitamin E produced small improvements in selected nerve-conduction velocities in diabetic neuropathy, while nerve amplitudes and HbA1c were unchanged; functional pain/gait outcomes remain insufficient.

Randomized crossover study in 20 healthy men found co-ingestion with non-fat fermented milk increased short-term bioavailability markers for vitamins A, D, E and K versus water; this is a food-matrix absorption finding, not evidence of superior clinical outcomes.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of 14 trials/715 patients found vitamin E was associated with less severe antineoplastic-treatment oral mucositis, with similar direction in pediatric and adult subgroups; formulation and administration differences across trials still matter.

Systematic review found no qualifying human clinical studies of vitamin E on cerebrovascular function; positive effects came entirely from heterogeneous preclinical models, so human cerebrovascular benefit is unestablished.

Randomized pilot comparing ketotifen with vitamin E in NAFLD found ketotifen produced greater improvements on several steatosis, glycemic and inflammatory measures; the active-comparator design does not establish vitamin E efficacy against placebo.

Three-arm randomized MASLD study found vitamin E and saroglitazar were not significantly better than lifestyle intervention alone for liver-stiffness, fibrosis-score or most secondary outcomes over 24 weeks.

Human pharmacokinetic study found vitamin E absorption depended on meal timing/second-meal fat exposure and was reduced in women with obesity/MASLD; evidence informs absorption physiology rather than supplement efficacy.

Four-month double-blind RCT in healthy vegans found a multinutrient plus omega-3 supplement increased omega-3 index and 25-OH-vitamin D, while doubling the omega-3/vitamin-D dose conferred no significant additional biomarker advantage; clinical endpoints were not tested.

Randomized placebo-controlled trial in 150 healthy adults found palm tocotrienol-rich fraction increased influenza-vaccine antibody and selected Th1/antioxidant responses across doses; immune-marker enhancement does not establish lower infection risk.

Network meta-analysis of COVID-19 nutrition RCTs found different supplements affected different inflammatory markers with mostly low or very-low certainty; heterogeneous interventions and surrogate outcomes preclude a single best-supplement recommendation.

Network meta-analysis suggested calcium, vitamin D and several multi-nutrient combinations may reduce preeclampsia risk, but indirect ranking evidence and combination regimens prevent attribution to vitamin C/E or any single ingredient.

Secondary analysis of a postpartum randomized cohort found maternal serum vitamins A, E and K and breastmilk A/E were generally adequate while vitamin-D sufficiency was less consistent; this informs postpartum status and milk transfer rather than a supplementation effect.
